feature: The build loop stops touching your app
summary: The unmanned loop now builds and launches its own copy of Photonz, called Photonz (Probe), whenever it needs to look at a running app. Your Photonz Dev app is no longer rebuilt, quit or relaunched behind your back, so a playtest session cannot be ended under you and macOS cannot be made to re-ask for Screen Recording.
setup: Nothing to install. queue/playtest.lock is the switch: while that file exists, the build script refuses to rebuild your dev app at all.

try.do: Leave Photonz Dev open and note its menu bar icon.
Read the refusal it prints, and check your app is still running.
Look at the menu bar: a second viewfinder icon appears, and its menu says Photonz (Probe).
Confirm your own app and its windows are exactly as you left them.
To rebuild your own app on purpose, delete queue/playtest.lock first.

evaluate: Is the refusal message clear enough that you know immediately what to do next?
Is queue/playtest.lock the right switch, or should the loop simply never rebuild your dev app whether or not a lock exists?
Is a second viewfinder icon in the menu bar acceptable while a runner is checking its work, or should the probe be invisible there?
Should deleting the lock be the normal way to rebuild your own app, or would you rather the lock expired on its own after a few hours?
rough: No script can stop a runner from typing pkill -f Photonz or opening your app directly. That is now written as a never-do in the runner contract and the run-app skill, and the skill no longer tells anyone to routinely kill the dev app, but it rests on the runner reading it.
The probe app re-asks for Screen Recording every time its binary changes, so anything that needs a real capture still needs you. The win is that it is never your grant being reset.
The probe build is the same release-configuration compile as a dev build, so a runner that wants a running app still waits about twenty seconds for it.
